scope.flow: ERC-4337 UserOp signature validation in AtomWallet._validateSignature via validateUserOp
scope.environment: ERC-4337 EntryPoint handleOps bundling with AtomWallet smart account

statements.text: A valid on-chain ECDSA signature from an AtomWallet owner is observable after any executed UserOp.
Any observer of a valid owner signature can derive a high-s counterpart with s' = curve_order - s and v' = v XOR 1, whose recovered address is identical to the original signer.
The adversary repeatedly submits griefing UserOps carrying the derived high-s signature targeting an AtomWallet.
During handleOps execution the EntryPoint calls validateUserOp without a try/catch.
The InvalidSignatureS branch of _validateSignature unconditionally reverts instead of returning SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED, and tryRecover rejects the high-s value.
An adversary can repeatedly submit griefing UserOps targeting any AtomWallet using the constructable high-s signature.
Bundler simulation of the griefing UserOp reverts, wasting bundler compute on every griefing submission.
In EntryPoint implementations where validation reverts propagate to the outer handleOps call, the bundler's entire batch transaction fails on-chain, causing gas loss.
Persistent griefing can cause bundlers to deprioritize or refuse to service the targeted AtomWallet, degrading the user's ability to submit transactions through ERC-4337.
On a signature mismatch, validateUserOp should return SIG_VALIDATION_FAILED (1) without reverting, so the EntryPoint can distinguish signature failure from a wallet bug.
High-s signatures are technically valid ECDSA and a high-s counterpart of any valid owner signature is constructable against any live wallet.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether the griefing UserOp was actually observed on-chain; impacts are described as potential/conditional.
Bundler retry/blacklist behavior (impact 2b) is conditional on bundler error handling and not separately extracted.
Whether validation revert propagates to handleOps is EntryPoint-version dependent.
